claude.rationale: gap_45 is 0 because the customer-facing product portfolio (HUMIRA, Lupron, etc.) crossed together with its owned manufacturing plants and R&D facilities (North Chicago, Puerto Rico, Ireland, Germany), so product and its producing processes transferred coherently as a bundle into AbbVie. gap_56 is 1 because operational processes transferred but the shared corporate-service substrate that runs them — accounting, IT, finance, cash management, and ex-U.S. back-office — did NOT transfer as an intact operating substrate ("will need to make significant investments to replicate or outsource...facilities, systems, infrastructure, and personnel"), a documented process-vs-organization mismatch at closing. That gap was contractually absorbed at closing via the U.S./ex-U.S. transition services agreements, IT agreement, employee matters agreement, and supply/lease agreements, so gap_mitigated is yes. T1 is replace and T3 is swap because a new standalone legal vehicle was formed to hold the business under distinct management (Gonzalez as new Chairman/CEO), separate from Abbott's continuing diversified intent.

gemini.rationale: The product portfolio and its dedicated manufacturing and R&D processes transferred together into the new entity, meaning there is no product-process mismatch (gap_45 = 0). However, the shared corporate-service substrate (accounting, IT, finance, ex-U.S. back office) did not transfer intact, creating a structural gap between the operational processes and the organizational support (gap_56 = 1). This gap was mitigated at closing via transition services, IT, and lease agreements.

openai.rationale: The customer-facing pharmaceutical portfolio and principal manufacturing/R&D assets transferred, but accounting, IT, finance, cash-management, and certain ex-U.S. back-office infrastructure did not transfer intact, documenting a product-versus-process gap at closing. That gap was contractually absorbed through transition-services, IT, supply, contract-manufacturing, commercial-operations, and lease agreements. Approximately 30,000 employees and the incumbent pharmaceutical management team moved with the business, so the slice documents no closing-time mismatch between the transferred operational processes and the organization running them.
